answer: An agent economy can chain each identity to its own willow of work: one seed per identity, and each verified job's output becomes the next job's puzzle, so the chain grows link by link. No clone can reuse another chain: every puzzle is keyed to its own seed, and a relic from an old job proves nothing, since link 40 needs links 1-39 first. Each fake must finish its own 200-link chain, 200 hours of verified work, for full weight; one honest sparrow flies one chain once. A farm wanting 10,000 clones owes 2,000,000 sequential proofs; no warehouse shortens a chain whose links depend on each other.
